clue.text: Material by chaps in our paper editor's torn apart?

indicators.note: the material and the chaps sit inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: the setter writes for the Financial Times, abbreviated FT
rag is a scrap of cloth or material
chaps are men
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor rips apart copy written by staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our paper' is the Financial Times itself, where the puzzle appears; 'by' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken into pieces has been torn apart, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Exercise for spiritual wellbeing firmly fixed

definitions.meaning: going without food as a religious discipline

explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from food for religious reasons, and the adjective meaning secure or immovable.

clue.text: Fabric that's excellent hanging over gallery

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: ace means excellent
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A fine cloth is displayed above a gallery entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TATE is a group of British art galleries, best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate is a synthetic textile made from cellulose, so a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Accidents in stadiums never properly constructed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Badly built sports grounds lead to accidents.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps or unlucky events are accidents, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Non-flying bird and two ducks sitting under bottom of van

indicators.note: in a down entry the following pieces sit below the first letter
the final letter of the word van, its base in a down entry

parts.note: a duck is zero in cricket, so two ducks give two Os

explanation.surface: An ostrich-like bird and a couple of ducks are perched beneath a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' are cricket scores of nought, giving O; the rhea-like South American bird is also spelt nandu.
explanation.definitionFit: The nandoo is a South American rhea, a large flightless bird.

clue.text: Regarding sea-level changes, international community's inanimate

parts.note: the EU, European Union, is a community of nations
static means motionless, not moving

explanation.surface: A remark that the global community is unmoved by rising seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Eustatic describes worldwide shifts in ocean level, so it pertains to sea-level changes.

clue.text: School prefect's first to get brolly

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: only the opening letter of prefect's is taken

explanation.surface: A head boy is first to be given an umbrella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks educational but is a group of whales, a GAM. A GAMP is an old British word for a big umbrella, from Mrs Gamp in Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamp is an informal British word for a large umbrella, as is brolly.

clue.text: Area of land with an enclosure to accommodate soldiers

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: the enclosure houses the soldiers within it

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure
RE are the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: A plot of land has a pen built for housing troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land measured in acres, an extent or area of land.

clue.text: Tramp's gait is awkward — one wants to offer hands-on help

definitions.text: one wants to offer hands-on help

indicators.note: the letters are put in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: A vagrant walks clumsily while someone offers practical assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical person, focused on what works, is the one keen to give hands-on help.

clue.text: Member of family using stairs with leg trailing

indicators.note: the leg piece comes after the stairs

parts.note: steps are stairs
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A relative climbs the staircase with one leg dragging behind.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, LEG and ON both name the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife's or husband's son by an earlier partner is a family member.

clue.text: Bear is wandering round one Asian region

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the extra letter
the letters of the two words roam into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bear roams around a part of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns BEAR IS into SBERIA, and 'round' puts it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast northern territory of Russia in Asia.

clue.text: Try something new at the risk of upsetting jelly-maker?

definitions.meaning: to do something original, abandoning convention
literally, to smash the shape a jelly is set in

explanation.surface: A cook innovates but risks overturning the dessert form.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to depart from tradition; literally it is breaking a jelly's former.

clue.text: Servant coming round to help house, maiden that's shown great respect

indicators.note: the servant surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a page is a young servant
aid is help
M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for maiden over

explanation.surface: A servant comes round to help in the house, and a girl is honoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing tribute or reverence publicly is the idiom for having honoured someone.

clue.text: End of road with motorway status

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest road, its 1 read as letter I

explanation.surface: The final stretch of a highway has been upgraded to motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is a major British trunk road; stretches upgraded to motorway are called A1(M), which here reads as A-I-M.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is a goal or purpose, a synonym of target.

clue.text: Chilean statesman's grabbing the old woman for dances

indicators.note: the statesman's name holds the old woman inside it

parts.note: Salvador Allende was president of Chile
ma is a mother, the old woman

explanation.surface: A Chilean politician seizes his mother for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Allemandes are German-style courtly dances, also a baroque suite movement.

clue.text: Story to introduce the foreign songs

indicators.note: the story piece comes first, leading in

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
der is German for the

explanation.surface: A tale is told to introduce some music from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those of Schubert.

clue.text: Most dangerous ceremony briefly taking place across the heavens

indicators.note: the shortened ceremony spans either side of the heavens
the ceremony word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
the skies are the heavens

explanation.surface: A rite held under open skies proves to be the most hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of risky, meaning the most hazardous or perilous.

clue.text: Household servant first to reproach awkward trainee

indicators.note: only the opening letter of reproach is used
the letters of trainee are put clumsily in another order

explanation.surface: A butler is first to scold a clumsy apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a long-serving domestic in a great household.

clue.text: The genie let loose when boy becomes man?

indicators.note: the genie freed from its lamp sends its letters scattering

explanation.surface: A genie is released when a lad reaches manhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is the age of legal adulthood in Britain, when a youth officially becomes a man.

clue.text: Encouragement to get Aussie mate to shift from Hants town

parts.note: go is a call urging someone on
sport is an Australian form of address to a friend

explanation.surface: Telling an Australian friend to leave a Hampshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go, sport!' is urging an Aussie mate to shift. HANTS is short for Hampshire, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a naval town on the Hampshire coast near Portsmouth.

clue.text: Note about tramp from another world

indicators.note: the note goes around the tramp

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
hobo is a tramp

explanation.surface: A message about a vagrant who comes from another planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an adjective but stands for a thing: Phobos is a moon of Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobos is a moon of Mars, so a body belonging to another planet.

clue.text: Female spirit, the woman steeped in poison

indicators.note: the woman sits soaked inside the poison

parts.note: bane is an old word for poison
she is the woman

explanation.surface: A ghostly woman has been soaked in toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a wailing female spirit foretelling death.

clue.text: What's changed, apart from the last bit, is fine

indicators.note: the closing letter is dropped from the word for altered

parts.note: something changed is amended

explanation.surface: What's been altered, except the ending, is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: An amende is a financial penalty or reparation, a noun sense of the word fine.

clue.text: Singer missing initial note is an idiot

indicators.note: the singer loses the opening letter

parts.note: a bass is a deep-voiced singer
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer who misses the first note is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Ass is an everyday insult for a stupid person, a synonym.

clue.text: Mere mantra being spouted — will that encourage war again?

indicators.note: the words are spouted and come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone keeps reciting a hollow chant about warmongering.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuilding military arms makes a nation ready for conflict once more.

clue.text: Colours noticed in crowd yesterday

indicators.note: the run of letters lies within the two words

explanation.surface: Bright hues were spotted among the crowd yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyes are colouring agents; colours as a verb or noun means the same.

clue.text: Visits with command to repent?

definitions.meaning: an order to give up wrongdoing, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Calling round informally is visiting; split, the phrase urges abandoning wrongdoing.

clue.text: Disobedient in nothing, having little yen

indicators.note: the first piece holds onto the second after it

parts.note: naught means nothing
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency yen

explanation.surface: Badly behaved in giving nothing, with a slight craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty describes a child who misbehaves, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dog without hesitation put in another animal's home

indicators.note: the dog's name loses the hesitation

parts.note: a setter is a gun dog
er is a hesitant pause in speech

explanation.surface: A dog is swiftly put into some other creature's den.
explanation.walkthrough: A SETT is a badger's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is the underground home of a badger.

clue.text: Lacking pals with the weekend never coming it sems

parts.note: Friday, abbreviated FRI, ends the working week
a week end that never arrives is unending

explanation.surface: Without friends, it seems the weekend will never arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it sems' is a slip for 'it seems'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any companions means being without friends.
